fields.why: The text's claims rest on percentages correct and chi-square tests (binary/categorical), but Table 2 reports the mean (SD) composite score for every group, and 'knowledge scores were higher' can be read off those means. Both lists are defensible; A records more of what the article shows.

The only equity content is one Discussion sentence on patients who 'lack access to specialty practitioners'; it is a determinant (both readers record it there), not a social-position group, so no dimension is needed for level 1. A's 'other' descriptor is defensible; the brief should say whether an access barrier named only in the discussion also gets a dimension entry.

brief_issues: No rule on whether an access-to-care remark with no measured group is an 'other' dimension or only a determinant_of_health. Outcome types for a bounded 0–3 score shown as mean (SD) but tested with chi-square on its distribution is also not settled.
